author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description through the visit form, reached at the visit's own address. A valid correction updates that visit in place and adds no visit; an invalid one is refused under the booking rules. Cancelling a visit stays out of scope (NG-5 narrowed).
acceptance_criteria: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, model attribute `visit`) prefilled with that visit's current date and description.

POST to the same address with a non-blank description and a date after today updates that visit in place: the stored visit carries the new date and description, the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the response redirects to the owner detail page.
POST with a blank description, or with a date of today or earlier, redisplays the visit form naming the offending field, and the stored visit keeps its earlier date and description.
Edge case 3: a visitId that does not belong to the named pet, a visitId that does not exist, or a petId that does not belong to the named owner is refused on both GET and POST, and no visit changes.
Edge case 4: the correction form offers the visit's own date, not the earliest date a booking would accept (tomorrow).
The owner detail page gains no edit link or other entry point to the correction in this slice.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, as narrowed).
An edit link or any other visible entry point on the owner record page: the owner deferred it to a follow-up request.
Relaxing the future-date rule so a past visit can be corrected as it stands: recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.
Moving a visit to another pet.
A confirmation message after a correction: not requested. Any new user-facing wording must satisfy REQ-LANG-002 (message bundles, every supported language).
notes: Owner-specified constraints (intake line 1 request): reuse pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute; validate like visit creation (description required, date in the future); the pet must not gain an additional visit record. Edge cases 3 and 4 are my decisions within that scope: refusal is the narrowest reading and mirrors booking edge case 1. anInvalidVisitCorrection... is one data-driven test over blank description, today, and a past date; aVisitCorrectionOutside... is one data-driven test over the three mismatch cases, GET and POST. Docs written this dispatch: docs/prd.md (NG-5 row narrowed, Non-Goals preamble, REQ-VIS-003 narrative, Done-when bullets, edge cases 3-4, two Open Questions), new docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-visit-correction-narrows-ng-5.md, and a status line on docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. The docs/adr/README.md index lacks a row for the new ADR; that file is outside my write scope. The reused template's heading and submit label read as creation wording; how the form presents a correction is design's call, within REQ-LANG-002.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A visit correction reuses three existing patterns with small adjustments. (1) Aggregate write path: system-design § Contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry': the correction enters through Owner, reaches the pet by Owner.getPet(Integer) and the visit through the pet, and saves through OwnerRepository by cascade. No VisitRepository, no Owner.addVisit. (2) Optional-path-variable model-attribute loader, as PetController.findPet (PetController.java:76) does for petId: VisitController's `visit` attribute becomes the stored visit when a visitId path variable is present, and stays a fresh visit attached to the pet for booking. (3) Create-or-update submit label, as createOrUpdateOwnerForm.html:18 switches addOwner/updateOwner on owner['new']. Adjustments: Pet gains a lookup of one of its visits by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:126). The VisitController binder gains an allow-list. The non-future-date check is shared by both handlers, not copied. One message key is added to every translated bundle. Basis: grep and file reads; the IDE oracle is not connected, so these symbol citations are the weaker basis.
integration_points: Model-attribute loader (VisitController.java:64): Spring runs the `visit` @ModelAttribute method before every handler in the class, the new GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit included. Add `@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId`. When present, return the stored visit from the pet's new visit lookup and attach nothing. When absent, keep today's booking behavior (new Visit added to the pet). Left unchanged, the loader attaches a new visit to the pet on every correction, which is the failure the requirement forbids.

Visit lookup on Pet: return one of the pet's persisted visits by identity, or null when none matches. Mirror Owner.getPet(Integer), skipping unsaved visits. Navigation lives on the aggregate, not in the controller (architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Aggregate row).

Refusal, edge case 3: an unknown owner, a pet of another owner, an unknown visitId, or a visitId of another pet makes the loader throw IllegalArgumentException, the same mechanism as booking edge case 1. It fires before binding on both GET and POST, so no write happens. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles § Realization, secret-disclosure row: the error page renders the message).

Binding target for the new POST entry point: the stored persisted Visit behind an allow-list. The class-wide @InitBinder keeps setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") and adds setAllowedFields("date", "description") (security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row). It also covers booking without changing it: date and description are Visit's only writable properties besides id, and the form's hidden petId and the tests' name parameter bind to nothing today.

Validation: the correction handler takes the same @Valid Visit (description @NotBlank) and the existing non-future-date check with the same field error code, typeMismatch.visitDate (VisitController.java:101). Move that check into one private method both handlers call; do not copy it. A copied rule is a fresh controller rule (architecture-principles § Web controller row and the paragraph after the catalog). Moving the rule into the domain is system-design Open Question 2 and outside this slice.

Write path: a valid correction calls owners.save(owner), whose merge cascades to the corrected visit, then returns "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}". It adds no flash message (prd-entry non-goal). Never reuse the booking's hard-coded 'Your visit has been booked'.

Transaction boundary: none on the handler. The loaded graph is detached because open-in-view is disabled (system-design § Persistence). A refused correction therefore leaves its bound values only on the discarded detached object. Do not annotate the handler @Transactional: dirty checking would then persist a refused correction (architecture-principles § Design Principles 7, fail secure).

Template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm): the heading already switches on visit['new'], so a correction reads 'Visit'. Change the submit button to th:with="text=${visit['new']} ? #{addVisit} : #{updateVisit}" th:text="${text}", mirroring createOrUpdateOwnerForm.html:18. The form has no th:action and posts to its own address, so the correction POST reaches /edit unchanged. The date input keeps th:min=${minVisitDate}; its value is the stored date (edge case 4).

Message key updateVisit: add to messages.properties and the nine translated bundles (de, es, fa, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr). messages_en.properties stays empty by design, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest skips it (REQ-LANG-002).

Repository boundary double: keep the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in the @WebMvcTest VisitControllerTests. This is a conscious framework-stub exception. OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, so a hand-written double would implement that whole surface, and the web slice loads no JPA for the real one (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Stub findById with a real Owner→Pet→Visit graph built from real entities with ids set.

Assertions through the stub: on success, verify save received the owner, the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the same visit instance carries the new date and description. On refusal and on invalid input, verify save was never called; 'the stored visit keeps its earlier values' is observed as nothing saved. Do not assert the in-memory visit's fields on the invalid path, because binding precedes validation and the detached object carries the rejected values by design.

Transport double: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). No exception handler exists, so the loader's IllegalArgumentException leaves perform() wrapped in a ServletException. The refusal test asserts that cause plus no save, as one data-driven test over the three mismatches on GET and POST, per the prd-entry notes.

patterns.description: model-attribute loader keyed on an optional path variable: fresh object when absent, stored entity found through the owner when present
lookup of a child by identity on its parent, null when absent; the shape for the pet's visit lookup
localized add/update submit label switched on the bound object's new-ness
the existing non-future-date rule, to be shared by booking and correction rather than copied

risks.risk: The unchanged class-wide loader attaches a phantom new visit on every correction, so the pet gains a visit and the save cascades a blank one.
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on the optional visitId. The success test asserts the saved pet's visit count is unchanged (system-design § Contracts, Invariants: a correction attaches no new visit).

risks.risk: On a refused correction the Previous Visits table renders the corrected visit with its rejected values, because the form and the table share the same object.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for this slice: nothing is stored and the form names the offending field (architecture-principles § Design Principles 7, fail secure: no partially-applied write).

risks.risk: Nine new translations written without a native reviewer; the key-sync test checks that keys are present, not that the wording is right.
risks.mitigation: Build each value from that bundle's own updateOwner verb and addVisit noun, so the phrasing tracks wording already confirmed in the bundle (system-design § Contracts, REQ-LANG-002 paragraph).

risks.risk: A refused correction surfaces as the generic error page with a server-error status, and that page renders the exception message (system-design § Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: Same mechanism and status as booking edge case 1, so the narrowest reading. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles § Realization, secret-disclosure row).

risks.risk: A new state-changing route open to any caller.
risks.mitigation: Matches the demonstration baseline for every edit route (system-design § Threat Model, unauthenticated-modification row; security-principles § Realization, widening-surface row). It exposes a visit's date and description for update. Each request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the path (security-principles § Realization, cross-request-state row).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Design-doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md adds REQ-VIS-003 to the Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController rows, updates the Pet and VisitController purposes, adds a correction invariant, adds visit identifiers to Security Context inputs, updates the mass-assignment and unvalidated-input threat rows, and adds a derived, unconfirmed Known Defects row for the gaps in the REQ-LANG-002 check. The REQ-LANG-002 paragraph now points at that row instead of claiming full enforcement. docs/adr/README.md adds the index row the product expert flagged for 2026-09-12-non-goal-visit-correction-narrows-ng-5.md and marks the 2026-08-08 row 'NG-5 narrowed 2026-09-12'. No ADR written: every pattern the slice uses already exists, and nothing here constrains later slices. Wording decision (flagged by the product expert): the heading already reads 'Visit' for a stored visit; only the submit label switches, to a new updateVisit key in every translated bundle. The heading's 'Visit' is a hard-coded literal that predates this slice. It is recorded as a Known Defect and not fixed here, because fixing it would add a second key outside the request. Open questions recorded rather than decided (no owner reply available): (a) whether a mismatched owner/pet/visit should answer not-found instead of the generic error page; booking edge case 1 has the same shape, so this slice mirrors it. (b) Whether the non-future-date rule moves from the controller into the domain; this is existing system-design Open Question 2, and the slice shares the rule without copying it, so the deviation does not grow.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: An empty date passes the correction route and wipes the stored visit's date. Attacker path, reachable by any caller and by a user who clears the date input: POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with `date=` and a non-blank description. Spring's formatter binds an empty string to a null LocalDate without a binding error. `rejectDateNotInFuture` guards with `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()))`, so a null date is not rejected. `Visit.java:38-40` `@Column(name = "visit_date") @DateTimeFormat(pattern = "yyyy-MM-dd") private LocalDate date;` has no @NotNull, and `db/h2/schema.sql:61` `visit_date  DATE,` is nullable. `owners.save(owner)` then persists the stored visit with no date. This breaks the PRD rule that a correction follows the booking rules, which require 'a date later than today' (docs/prd.md:105, :108, :110). The weakness already exists on the booking route (POST /visits/new, same helper), where it creates a visit with no date. This slice extends it to overwriting an existing visit's date. The tests do not cover it: grep -F 'param("date"' finds only non-empty values (VisitControllerTests.java:157, :178), and the invalidCorrections cases pass date.toString(). Harm is limited to data integrity on one field; there is no confidentiality or code-execution impact, so this is not a security block. I did not run a test to exercise it; the null-binding step is reasoned from Spring's formatter contract. Question for the product expert: should a missing date be refused naming the date field? And if so, on the correction route only (the slice's route), or also on booking? Refusing it in the shared helper also changes the booking route (REQ-VIS-001), which this slice does not name, so it is not tagged autofix.

approved_aspects: Ownership chain enforced per request, satisfying the brief's 'Trusting cross-request state' row. VisitController.java:66-70 re-resolves the owner by ownerId and the pet by `owner.getPet(petId)`. The new branch reaches the visit only through `pet.getVisit(visitId)`, and an unknown visit throws IllegalArgumentException before any save. Pet.getVisit (Pet.java:90-96) skips unsaved visits and matches by id within this pet only. VisitControllerTests covers GET and POST for another pet's visit, an unknown visit, and another owner's pet, asserting `save` is never called.

The binder is strengthened, not weakened (Pattern Consistency, removed-check rule). VisitController.java:53-54 keeps `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` and adds `setAllowedFields("date", "description")`. The @InitBinder has no attribute name, so it also applies to the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` parameter of both POST handlers. That closes a pre-existing path where extra form fields (owner name, address, telephone, nested pet fields) could be bound onto the unvalidated Owner and cascaded by the save. No mass-assignment surface is added.

Refused corrections do not persist. application.properties sets `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`, so the Owner graph loaded by `findById` is detached when binding runs. The handler comment's claim holds: bound values reach the database only through the explicit `owners.save(owner)`, which runs only when `result.hasErrors()` is false.

Output escaping unchanged and intact. createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:39-40 sets the button label with `th:with`/`th:text` from message keys (escaped). The description and date render through the existing inputField fragment and `th:text`. There is no th:utext, no `__${...}__` preprocessing, and no request-derived text in any expression. The ten added `updateVisit=` bundle values contain no markup (git diff -U0 of src/main/resources/messages/).

Error disclosure within the brief. The new IllegalArgumentException message (VisitController.java:86-87) carries only the three integer path ids, typed int/Integer so non-numeric input fails conversion first. error.html:18 renders it through escaped `th:text`, which matches the existing Owner/Pet-not-found pattern (VisitController.java:67-73). No credential or internal detail appears.

The added endpoints stay within the demonstration baseline (docs/security-principles.md). They are open like every other route, and system-design.md § Security Context and § Threat Model were updated to name visit identifiers as inputs and the correction route. No management exposure changes.

Supply chain: `git diff --stat -- build.gradle pom.xml gradle/ settings.gradle` is empty, so no dependency changed. No NVD match ran (grep for dependencyCheck in build.gradle finds nothing). Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

No hardcoded secrets, shell execution, file I/O, deserialization, logging, or query construction in the production diff. I read the full hunks of Pet.java, VisitController.java, the visit template, and the bundles.

author: system-design-expert
answer: (1) Carried. docs/system-design.md now mirrors the line-22 PRD change in three places. The VisitController Contracts row reads 'rejecting non-future dates on both and a missing date on correction'. The Threat Model 'Unvalidated input reaching persistence' row adds the correction route's missing-date refusal and qualifies the mitigation: a booking with no visit date is still stored, linked to the PRD open question. Open Question 2 records the placement below. The gate can run. (2) Placement: your proposal stands. Put a private check in VisitController that only processVisitCorrectionForm calls, separate from rejectDateNotInFuture. When visit.getDate() is null it calls result.rejectValue("date", "required"). Use the error code `required` and no other. It is the code PetValidator already uses for a missing birthDate (system-design § Constants, REQUIRED row), and the key is present in all ten translated bundles; messages_en stays empty by design (REQ-LANG-002). Classification, by the brief as written: architecture-principles.md:91 defines a business rule as one that holds at every entry point. Per the line-22 answer, booking still records a visit with no date and the PRD leaves that open. So presence of `date` holds on correction only, which makes it the correction request's shape, and the Web controller row (:85) counts request shape as binding. That means checklist item :144 does not trip, and the change does not extend the recorded deviation. Rejected alternatives: the shared helper or @NotNull on Visit.date would change booking, which the product answer forbids. A bean-validation group would add a marker type and a second validation mechanism for one route, against Design Principle 2 (consistency over novelty). A correction-only Form validator misreads that catalog row, which covers rules of the bound type, and a null date is not a rule of Visit while booking accepts it. The shared helper's contract is unchanged, so the return trigger in the line-18 design-block notes does not fire. Mechanics: an empty or whitespace-only `date` parameter binds to null with no binding error. The new check fires, and the shared helper skips null, so the date carries exactly one field error. A malformed date is a typeMismatch binding error that leaves the stored date on the object, so the new check does not fire for it. With no save, the stored visit keeps its values (fail secure, architecture-principles Design Principle 7). Doubles and binding target are unchanged from design-block line 18: MockMvc, @MockitoBean OwnerRepository, and the date/description allow-list. Your test plan fits. The 'no date' case asserts the field error code `required` on `date`, the form view, and no save. The booking pin (no-date booking still redirects) holds REQ-VIS-001 unchanged, as the product answer requires. (3) Recorded in Open Question 2: the refusal holds on correction only, is request shape, and sits outside the deviation. If the PRD refuses a no-date booking too, the rule holds at every entry point and belongs on Visit, and the controller check goes away. No ADR: the principle already lives in architecture-principles.md:91, and this slice contains the choice (adr-template § When to Create an ADR).
